## Answer

**Service: `mysql`, Operation: `SQL SELECT`**

Comparing the fastest (669.6ms, trace `3f185804...`) and slowest (797.4ms, trace `2e5db112...`) `/dispatch` traces from the frontend service:

| Operation (service / span) | Fast trace self-time | Slow trace self-time | Δ (extra time) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **mysql / SQL SELECT** | 285,311µs | 360,512µs | **+75,201µs** |
| redis-manual / GetDriver (aggregate) | 174,985µs | 201,946µs | +26,961µs |
| redis-manual / FindDriverIDs | 13,428µs | 33,903µs | +20,475µs |
| route / /route (aggregate) | 183,435µs | 190,292µs | +6,857µs |
| (all other spans) | — | — | roughly flat/negative |

Total extra time in the slow trace vs. fast: ~127.9ms. The single `mysql SQL SELECT` span (invoked once per trace, inside the `customer` service's `/customer` call) alone accounts for **~75.2ms of that gap — about 59% of the total slowdown**, making it by far the largest single contributor. This far outweighs the cumulative effect of the many repeated `redis-manual GetDriver` calls in the driver-lookup loop, even though those add up to a larger *count* of spans.
